# v14 _native.pyi generation

The committed `cc_transcript/_native.pyi` is MACHINE-GENERATED (user decision 2026-07-14, superseding the spec's hand-maintenance fallback): `cargo run -p cc-transcript-py --bin stub_gen` regenerates it; the drift gate runs both ways — `committed_stub_matches_generator_output` (cargo test in the stub_gen bin, byte-for-byte committed == regenerated, sharing the bin's `render()`) and `tests/test_native_stub.py` (stub == built extension name-for-name: modules, properties, methods, bases, constructibility via `__new__`, `__text_signature__` params — catches items the annotation sweep missed, which the generator alone can never see).

**Why a custom writer over plain pyo3-stub-gen `generate()`:** the extension is one flat namespace (`cc_transcript._native`) whose pyclasses deliberately claim facade module strings (`module = "cc_transcript.models"` etc.) for reprs, pickling, and griffe docs resolution. pyo3-stub-gen groups stub output by those module strings: it would emit per-facade `__init__.py` re-export shims over our hand-written facades (models.py, tools.py) and refuses the pure-Rust single-file layout for multi-module inventories. The bin (`rust/crates/py/src/bin/stub_gen.rs`) merges every module group into one `Module`, then post-processes: de-qualifies references to merged class names (per-name `\bgroup\.Name\b` regex so facade-only aliases like `cc_transcript.tools.ToolCall` stay qualified), drops group imports with no remaining qualified use, de-raws `#[getter(r#type)]` idents (pyo3-stub-gen 0.23 renders the Rust raw-ident prefix verbatim — invalid Python), types every `__match_args__` classattr as `typing.ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]` (MemberDef mutation), and enriches EventList programmatically with its `collections.abc.Sequence[TranscriptEvent]` base plus int/slice `__getitem__` overloads (ClassDef.bases push + cloned MethodDefs with `is_overload: true` — the generate:: structs are all public and constructible).

**Annotation rules (all-or-nothing per class):**
- Every `#[pyclass]` gets `#[pyo3_stub_gen::derive::gen_stub_pyclass]`; every `#[pymethods]` gets `#[pyo3_stub_gen::derive::gen_stub_pymethods]`. A gen_stub_pymethods block whose class lacks gen_stub_pyclass panics the gatherer ("Missing struct_id/enum_id") — and getters RETURNING an unregistered view type fail compile with `PyStubType not satisfied`, so partial sweeps don't even build.
- Getters returning `PyAny`/`PyTuple`/`PyDict` carry `#[gen_stub(override_return_type(type_repr = "...", imports = (...)))]` with the precise type; parameters that lack `PyStubType` (e.g. `&[u8]`) carry `#[gen_stub(override_type(type_repr = "bytes"))]`. Convention: type_reprs use the fully qualified runtime module string (`cc_transcript.models.EntryMeta`); the writer normalizes merged names, and non-merged facade refs (cc_transcript.ids branded NewTypes, alias unions in tools/models) render qualified with their import retained.
- Known pyo3-stub-gen 0.23 misrender: `Option<Vec<T>>` / `Option<HashMap<..>>` / `Option<(A, B)>` in `#[pyo3(signature = (... = None))]` params and returns push the Option INSIDE the container (`Sequence[str | None]` for `Option<Vec<String>>`) — override those sites explicitly.
- `view_dunders!` registers only its `__match_args__` classattr; the repr/eq/copy/deepcopy dunders carry `#[gen_stub(skip)]` and the `@hash` arm's block is unannotated, so ~50 view classes don't each grow five noise dunders. Flipping this on required EVERY view_dunders class to be gen_stub_pyclass-registered first, so it went last in the adoption sweep (now complete — every pyclass/pymethods/pyfunction in the crate is registered).

**Accepted divergences from the hand-written seed (gen matches runtime better):** no `/` positional-only markers (pyo3 params are positional-or-keyword), `Sequence[T]` where pyo3 extraction accepts any sequence, `__new__` instead of `__init__` (great-docs' `_INIT_DUNDERS` filter already hides both), real default values instead of `...`, and an extra typed `__reversed__` on EventList.

**Spike facts (2026-07-14):** pyo3-stub-gen 0.23.0 works under pyo3 0.28 + abi3-py313 + `multiple-pymethods` + `extends =` chains + `frozen`; docstrings (Attributes: sections) flow verbatim; `#[new]` → typed `__new__`; non-subclass classes get `@typing.final`. The old claim that stub-gen "cannot generate this stub" was a never-run hunch inherited from a dead agent.
